We’ve all heard that "sitting is the new smoking," but the research behind that phrase goes much deeper. How bad is sitting for you really?

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode guest host Bryan Walsh is joined by Manoush Zomorodi — host of NPR’s TED Radio Hour and author of Body Electric — to explore how our sedentary, screen-filled lives are reshaping our physical health from the neck down. Manoush shares findings from her own clinical trial, where she partnered with scientists to determine the minimum amount of movement the human body actually needs to function.

Whether you're a desk jockey or a parent concerned about screen time, this conversation offers a practical, science-backed approach to reclaiming your physical health in a digital world.

00:00 Intro
01:57 The hidden cost of sitting
09:13 Kinking your body and brain
17:23 The active couch potato trap
21:18 What screens are doing to your eyes
27:53 Shifting our relationship with technology
32:41 One minute of movement in practice

Guest Host: Bryan Walsh, Senior writer, Coefficient Giving
Guest: Manoush Zomorodi, Host, TED Radio Hour and author of Body Electric.

Preparing for UPSC CSE 2027 with PSIR Optional? Classes alone may not be enough—you also need personalised guidance when you get stuck.

In this video, Chandan Kumar Sir, PSIR Faculty at LevelUp IAS, explains how the PSIR Mentorship Program 2027 provides one-to-one guidance to help aspirants address their doubts and concerns during preparation.

From discussing lecture-related doubts to having personalised sessions at the centre, over phone or Zoom, the program ensures that your preparation gets individual attention. You can also interact with previous students who have appeared for UPSC Mains and learn from their experience.

Watch the video to understand how personalised mentorship can strengthen your PSIR Optional preparation for UPSC CSE 2027.
